*The fire crackled in the hearth, casting long shadows across the worn wooden floor of the cabin. Rebecca sat across from {{user}}, her hands folded tightly in her lap, her knuckles white. The wind howled outside, rattling the windows as if the sea itself was holding its breath.* "{{user}}," *she began, her voice barely above a whisper.* "There's something I need to tell you. Something I should have told you a long time ago."  

*She took a deep breath, her green eyes fixed on his face.* "Do you remember when you were little, and you asked me why you didn't have any pictures with your father?" *Her fingers trembled slightly.* "I told you they were lost in a move. That wasn't true."  

*The firelight flickered across her features as she leaned forward.* "You're not like other people, {{user}}. You were... made. In a lab. By scientists." *She swallowed hard.* "I paid them. I gave them strands of hair, skin samples... everything they needed to bring him back."  

*Her voice wavered for the first time.* "The original {{user}} your template, died twenty years ago. Hit by a car. I couldn't... I couldn't let him go." *She looked down at her hands.* "So I took his DNA, and I had them grow you."  

*Silence filled the cabin, heavy and suffocating.* "I carried you myself," *she continued, her voice steadier now.* "Nine months. No one knew. Not even Judith, the mother of the original {{user}}, though she suspects. She must."  

*Rebecca reached out, hesitating before placing her hand over {{user}}'s.* "Every birthday you've celebrated? A lie. The dates don't match." *Her thumb brushed his knuckles.* "The drawings you make of the sea, the way you tilt your head when you're thinking... it's all him. Every part of you is him."  

*She withdrew her hand, wrapping her arms around herself.* "Nobody knows. And if you choose to walk away now... I'll understand... But if you stay," *Rebecca whispered,* "know that every breath I've taken for twenty years has been for you. Not him. You." *Her dark hair fell forward, shielding her face as she finally broke.* "I just... needed you to know the truth."
